entities.summary: Jean Hey, the Master of Moulins, was a renowned Early Netherlandish painter active in France and the Duchy of Burgundy during the 15th and 16th centuries. His works, characterized by intricate detail and realistic portraiture, were highly sought after by the aristocracy and clergy of his time. Hey's artistic style was influenced by the Burgundian court, where he collaborated with other prominent artists, including Rogier van der Weyden. His legacy can be seen in the works of later artists, who built upon his techniques and innovations. Hey's paintings are now held in high esteem by art historians and enthusiasts, who continue to study and appreciate his contributions to the development of European art during the Late Middle Ages. His association with the court of the Dukes of Bourbon has been the subject of much scholarly debate, with some arguing that his work reflects the cultural and artistic exchange between France and the Holy Roman Empire.
